changes.current_line: Customers see an average uplift in authorization rates with Authorization Boost and Adaptive Acceptance.
changes.change: For payments leads reviewing acceptance: lead with the customer's own approvals, market by market. Show their approval rate in each country, the reasons behind their declines, and the money left on the table in each market, in a form they can hand to their CFO. Say 'approvals', not 'authorization'. Use the cross-customer average uplift only as supporting context, never as the headline.
changes.why: The buyer answered the average uplift deck with 'that's an average. What's mine?' and said 'I can't take an average to my CFO.', and he talks about 'approvals' and 'Money left on the table.', not authorization features.

changes.current_line: Support plans with tiered response times, up to 24/7 coverage.
changes.change: For accounts with a dedicated payments owner: a named person at Stripe who reviews your approvals every month, by market, and tells you what they found and what can be fixed, before you have to ask.
changes.why: The buyer asked who at Stripe looks at his numbers every month and the rep had no name, he called the per-market analysis the most useful thing we had sent him, and he said 'I heard from Stripe when I said I was leaving.'

changes.change: For buyers weighing local acquiring (the 'Local cards, local rails.' argument): answer with a per-country view of their own approvals and the reasons behind each market's declines. Offer it before a competitor proposes a test on their traffic, and deliver it while the test is still running.
changes.why: Adyen won by running a test on the customer's international traffic with results by country, and our market-by-market view with reasons arrived three weeks after he asked, when the test was already finished.

changes.change: Opener for existing customers whose payments owner has changed: a proactive review of your approvals by country, done for you, so your first look at your declines by market is one we bring you. Use this instead of the global positioning line.
changes.why: The evaluation started when a new head of payments replaced the departed buyer and 'the first thing he did was pull declines by country.', an analysis we never saw.
